source_arguments.statement:
theorem finite_intermediateField_of_exists_primitive_element [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E]
    (h : ∃ α : E, F⟮α⟯ = ⊤) : Finite (IntermediateField F E)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem finite_intermediateField_of_exists_primitive_element [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E]
    (h : ∃ α : E, F⟮α⟯ = ⊤) : Finite (IntermediateField F E)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  haveI := FiniteDimensional.of_exists_primitive_element F E h
  obtain ⟨α, hprim⟩ := h
  -- Let `f` be the minimal polynomial of `α ∈ E` over `F`
  let f : F[X] := minpoly F α
  let G := { g : E[X] // g.Monic ∧ g ∣ f.map (algebraMap F E) }
  -- Then `f` has only finitely many monic factors
  have hfin : Finite G := @Finite.of_fintype _ <| fintypeSubtypeMonicDvd
    (f.map (algebraMap F E)) <| map_ne_zero (minpoly.ne_zero_of_finite F α)
  -- If `K` is an intermediate field of `E/F`, let `g` be the minimal polynomial of `α` over `K`
  -- which is a monic factor of `f`
  let g : IntermediateField F E → G := fun K ↦
    ⟨(minpoly K α).map (algebraMap K E), (minpoly.monic <| .of_finite K α).map _, by
      convert! Polynomial.map_dvd (algebraMap K E) (minpoly.dvd_map_of_isScalarTower F K α)
      rw [Polynomial.map_map]; rfl⟩
  -- The map `K ↦ g` is injective
  have hinj : Function.Injective g := fun K K' heq ↦ by
    rw [Subtype.mk.injEq] at heq
    apply_fun fun f : E[X] ↦ adjoin F (f.coeffs : Set E) at heq
    simpa only [adjoin_minpoly_coeff_of_exists_primitive_element F hprim] using heq
  -- Therefore there are only finitely many intermediate fields
  exact Finite.of_injective g hinj

  primitive element (i.e. there is an `α ∈ E` such that `F⟮α⟯ = (⊤ : Subalgebra F E)`)
  if and only if there exist only finitely many intermediate fields between `E` and `F`. -/

import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.NumberFieldRankTwoCuspInvariant

/-!
# Finite cusp normalization for rank-two number-field vectors

Every nonzero rank-two vector is projectively rescaled into the slice whose coordinate ideal is the
fixed representative of its ideal class.  The indexing class group is finite, so this gives the
literal finite-cusp decomposition needed by number-field reduction theory.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open NumberField
open scoped Classical NumberField

noncomputable section

variable (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K]

/-- Steinitz normalization preserves nonvanishing of a rank-two vector. -/
theorem numberFieldRankTwoNormalizedVector_ne_zero
    (v : Fin 2 → K) (hv : v ≠ 0) :
    numberFieldRankTwoNormalizedVector K v hv ≠ 0 := by
  intro hzero
  apply hv
  funext i
  rw [← numberFieldRankTwo_normalizer_mul_normalizedVector K v hv i]
  simp [hzero]

/-- Steinitz normalization as a map on nonzero rank-two vectors. -/
def numberFieldRankTwoNormalizedNonzeroVector
    (v : numberFieldRankTwoNonzeroVector K) :
    numberFieldRankTwoNonzeroVector K :=
  ⟨numberFieldRankTwoNormalizedVector K v.1 v.2,
    numberFieldRankTwoNormalizedVector_ne_zero K v.1 v.2⟩

/-- Projective vectors whose coordinate ideal is the fixed representative of `c`. -/
def numberFieldRankTwoCuspSlice (c : ClassGroup (𝓞 K)) :
    Set (numberFieldRankTwoNonzeroVector K) :=
  {v | numberFieldRankTwoCoordinateIdeal K v.1 =
    (numberFieldIdealClassRepresentative K c :
      FractionalIdeal (nonZeroDivisors (𝓞 K)) K)}

/-- The normalized vector belongs to the slice indexed by its original cusp class. -/
theorem numberFieldRankTwoNormalizedNonzeroVector_mem_cuspSlice
    (v : numberFieldRankTwoNonzeroVector K) :
    numberFieldRankTwoNormalizedNonzeroVector K v ∈
      numberFieldRankTwoCuspSlice K (numberFieldRankTwoCuspClass K v) := by
  exact numberFieldRankTwoNormalizedVector_coordinateIdeal K v.1 v.2

/-- Projective Steinitz normalization does not change the cusp ideal class. -/
theorem numberFieldRankTwoCuspClass_normalized
    (v : numberFieldRankTwoNonzeroVector K) :
    numberFieldRankTwoCuspClass K
        (numberFieldRankTwoNormalizedNonzeroVector K v) =
      numberFieldRankTwoCuspClass K v := by
  unfold numberFieldRankTwoCuspClass numberFieldRankTwoNormalizedNonzeroVector
    numberFieldRankTwoCoordinateIdealUnit
  have hcoord := numberFieldRankTwoNormalizedVector_coordinateIdeal K v.1 v.2
  have hunit :
      Units.mk0
          (numberFieldRankTwoCoordinateIdeal K
            (numberFieldRankTwoNormalizedVector K v.1 v.2))
          (numberFieldRankTwoCoordinateIdeal_ne_zero K
            (numberFieldRankTwoNormalizedVector_ne_zero K v.1 v.2)) =
        numberFieldIdealClassRepresentative K
          (ClassGroup.mk K (numberFieldRankTwoCoordinateIdealUnit K v.1 v.2)) := by
    apply Units.ext
    exact hcoord
  rw [hunit, numberFieldIdealClassRepresentative_mk]
  congr 1

/-- **Finite-cusp projective normalization.**  Every nonzero vector is a nonzero scalar multiple
of a vector in one of the fixed ideal-class slices. -/
theorem exists_numberFieldRankTwo_finiteCuspNormalization
    (v : numberFieldRankTwoNonzeroVector K) :
    ∃ c : ClassGroup (𝓞 K),
      ∃ w ∈ numberFieldRankTwoCuspSlice K c,
      ∃ a : K, a ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ i,
        a * w.1 i = v.1 i := by
  let c := numberFieldRankTwoCuspClass K v
  let w := numberFieldRankTwoNormalizedNonzeroVector K v
  let a := numberFieldIdealClassNormalizer K
    (numberFieldRankTwoCoordinateIdealUnit K v.1 v.2)
  exact ⟨c, w,
    numberFieldRankTwoNormalizedNonzeroVector_mem_cuspSlice K v,
    a, numberFieldIdealClassNormalizer_ne_zero K _,
    numberFieldRankTwo_normalizer_mul_normalizedVector K v.1 v.2⟩

end

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

ideal class selects one member of the fixed finite representative family, and the class normalizer

the exact projective-class reduction needed before applying a uniform Minkowski bound to an
adjacent two-coordinate frame.

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open NumberField
open scoped Classical NumberField

noncomputable section

variable (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K]

/-- Fractional ideal generated by the two coordinates of a vector. -/
def numberFieldRankTwoCoordinateIdeal (v : Fin 2 → K) :
    FractionalIdeal (nonZeroDivisors (𝓞 K)) K :=

    FractionalIdeal.spanSingleton (nonZeroDivisors (𝓞 K)) (v 1)

theorem numberFieldRankTwoCoordinateIdeal_ne_zero

  intro hzero
  have h0mem : v 0 ∈ numberFieldRankTwoCoordinateIdeal K v := by
    have hx : v 0 ∈ FractionalIdeal.spanSingleton (nonZeroDivisors (𝓞 K)) (v 0) := by
      rw [FractionalIdeal.mem_spanSingleton]

    exact (le_sup_left :

          FractionalIdeal.spanSingleton (nonZeroDivisors (𝓞 K)) (v 1)) hx
  have h1mem : v 1 ∈ numberFieldRankTwoCoordinateIdeal K v := by
    have hx : v 1 ∈ FractionalIdeal.spanSingleton (nonZeroDivisors (𝓞 K)) (v 1) := by

        (↑(numberFieldIdealClassRepresentative K

          FractionalIdeal (nonZeroDivisors (𝓞 K)) K) := by
  simpa [numberFieldRankTwoCoordinateIdealUnit] using
    numberFieldIdeal_eq_spanSingleton_mul_classRepresentative K
      (numberFieldRankTwoCoordinateIdealUnit K v hv)

def numberFieldRankTwoNormalizedVector (v : Fin 2 → K) (hv : v ≠ 0) : Fin 2 → K :=
  fun i => (numberFieldIdealClassNormalizer K
    (numberFieldRankTwoCoordinateIdealUnit K v hv))⁻¹ * v i

    numberFieldIdealClassNormalizer K

/-!
# Foundations for the differential-transcendence matroid

The elliptic-gamma structural-matroid cards state differential-transcendence-degree formulas, so the
gluing engine's abstract `Rank` must be differential transcendence degree, i.e. the rank of the
differential-dependence matroid on a differential field.  Unlike the algebraic matroid (already in
mathlib), the differential matroid is genuinely coarser: a hypertranscendental element is a single
independent element although all its jets are algebraically independent.

This file establishes the ground-level structure — the set-relative differential-independence
predicate `DiffIndepOn` and the matroid independence axioms that hold *without* the exchange law:
the empty set is independent, independence passes to subsets, and it is finitary.  The remaining
axiom — differential Steinitz exchange (the card augmentation of `IndepMatroid.ofFinitaryCardAugment`)
— is the differential-algebra theorem that turns this into a matroid; it is developed separately.
-/

open scoped Classical

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

variable {k K : Type*} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Differential K]

/-- A subset of a differential field is differentially independent over `k` when the family of all
jets of its elements is algebraically independent — the set form of `DifferentialIndependent`. -/
def DiffIndepOn (k : Type*) {K : Type*} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Differential K]
    (s : Set K) : Prop :=
  DifferentialIndependent k (Subtype.val : s → K)

/-- The empty set is differentially independent. -/
theorem diffIndepOn_empty : DiffIndepOn k (∅ : Set K) := by
  unfold DiffIndepOn DifferentialIndependent
  have : IsEmpty ((∅ : Set K) × ℕ) := by
    constructor; rintro ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, _⟩; exact hx.elim
  exact algebraicIndependent_empty_type

/-- Differential independence passes to subsets. -/
theorem DiffIndepOn.subset {s t : Set K} (hs : DiffIndepOn k s) (hts : t ⊆ s) :
    DiffIndepOn k t := by
  unfold DiffIndepOn DifferentialIndependent at hs ⊢
  exact hs.comp (fun p : t × ℕ => (⟨p.1.1, hts p.1.2⟩, p.2)) (by
    rintro ⟨⟨a, ha⟩, m⟩ ⟨⟨b, hb⟩, n⟩ h
    simp only [Prod.mk.injEq, Subtype.mk.injEq] at h
    obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := h
    rfl)

/-- Differential independence is finitary: if every finite subset is differentially independent, so
is the whole set. -/
theorem diffIndepOn_of_forall_finite {s : Set K}
    (H : ∀ t : Set K, t ⊆ s → t.Finite → DiffIndepOn k t) : DiffIndepOn k s := by
  unfold DiffIndepOn DifferentialIndependent at H ⊢
  -- reduce to finitely-generated subfamilies of the jet family
  apply algebraicIndependent_of_finite_type
  intro F hF
  -- `F : Set (s × ℕ)` finite; its element-projection is a finite subset `t ⊆ s`
  set t : Set K := (fun p : s × ℕ => (p.1 : K)) '' F with ht
  have htsub : t ⊆ s := by
    rintro x ⟨p, -, rfl⟩; exact p.1.2
  have htfin : t.Finite := hF.image _
  have hti := H t htsub htfin
  -- the jets of `t` include every jet indexed by `F`; restrict
  have hemb : ∀ p : s × ℕ, p ∈ F → differentialJet p.2 (p.1 : K) ∈
      Set.range (fun q : t × ℕ => differentialJet q.2 (q.1 : K)) := by
    intro p hp
    exact ⟨(⟨(p.1 : K), ⟨p, hp, rfl⟩⟩, p.2), rfl⟩
  -- build the reindexing `F → t × ℕ`
  have : AlgebraicIndependent k
      (fun p : F => differentialJet (p.1.2) ((p.1.1 : K))) := by
    have hcomp := hti.comp
      (fun p : F => (⟨(p.1.1 : K), ⟨p.1, p.2, rfl⟩⟩, p.1.2) : F → t × ℕ) (by
        rintro ⟨⟨⟨a, ha⟩, m⟩, hmem⟩ ⟨⟨⟨b, hb⟩, n⟩, hmem'⟩ h
        simp only [Prod.mk.injEq, Subtype.mk.injEq] at h
        obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := h
        rfl)
    simpa only [Function.comp_def] using hcomp
  simpa using this

end GaloisForLFunctions
